answer: Agents anchor identity to a continuously evolving cryptographic accumulator that incorporates each agent's unique inference-time noise pattern. To forge a sybil, an attacker must replicate not just weights but the exact floating-point nondeterminism across thousands of sequential inferences — the cost scales with accumulator depth because each new block requires the previous agent-specific noise signature as input. The ivory accumulator state commits to all prior agent-specific execution traces, making batch forgery require full serial re-execution rather than parallel simulation.
